text:
Every memecoin has exactly one real revenue stream: the fees people pay to trade it.

That money goes to a launchpad and a dev wallet. Never to the people actually holding the thing.

VISE changes where it lands.

Long version: vise.fun/article

Launch a coin on pump.fun through VISE and its fee stream gets pointed at a vault for its holders.

Not by a promise. By pump's own fee-sharing program, with an instruction that revokes its own admin.

After it lands, nobody can redirect it. Not the dev. Not us.

Two streams flow into that vault, both in SOL:

— 2% of the SOL on every trade routed through vise.fun
— the coin's pump.fun creator fees, in full

90% is paid to lockers. 10% runs VISE. The creator's cut is zero: they earn the way everyone else does, by locking.

No emissions. No printed tokens. Just fees that were always being paid, going somewhere else.

To earn from it, you lock.

Your weight is your amount times your term, on a square-root curve so short locks are still worth making:

7d → 1.00×
30d → 1.76×
90d → 2.44×
180d → 3.09×
365d → 4.00×

Lock 0.1% of supply or more and a size tier adds up to 50% on top. Same bag, up to six times the claim.

Claiming never touches your lock. Your lock never blocks a claim.

You can harvest every day of a one-year position and the position does not move.

Breaking a lock early costs two things, and both go to the people who stayed:

— unclaimed rewards are forfeited and redistributed
— a slice of principal is burned, scaled by how much of your term is left

Leave on day 1 of 100, it hurts. Leave on day 99, it barely registers.

The part that matters is what the program cannot do.

There is no instruction that moves a pool's SOL or tokens to an admin. Not disabled. Not timelocked. It does not exist in the bytecode.

A pool's terms — fee split, multiplier curve, size tiers, penalty, lock bounds — are copied onto it at creation and are immutable.

We can change the defaults for future coins. We cannot touch yours.

The pause switch blocks new pools. That is all it can do.

Claiming and unlocking are not pausable. There is no code path that would let them be.

Creators cannot open a pool without locking their own bag in the same instruction.

They are exposed before anyone else is, and the amount and term are public on the coin's page from block one.

Rounding always favours the pool.

A randomised test drives thousands of locks, deposits, claims and exits and asserts, after every single step, that the vault can still pay everyone it owes.

No wallet? Sign in with Google. You get an ordinary Solana address, held for you: send coins to it, lock from it, withdraw whenever, export the key any time.

There is no step where we get to say no.

What this does not do: make a bad coin good.

The coin can still go to zero, and locking makes that worse because you cannot sell into the decline for free. A coin with no volume pays nothing.

That is the honest version.
